About.Name: Thomas Robertson
About.AboutText:
Hi, I am Thomas Robertson. I am a computer science student with an interest in software development and programming. I am pursuing a bachelor of arts at Seattle Pacific University. I am expanding my knowledge and skills in a variety of areas of computer science.

I enjoy examining new ways to code and I prefer to work in well-managed collaborative environments.

Outside of class, I spend most of my time reading whatever is at hand. I believe that learning new things is a critical part of life, and try to do so when I have the time.

Experience.EducationText: I graduated summa cum laude from SPU's Bachelor of Arts program, with a major in computer science.
Experience.EmploymentText: Having recently graduated from university, I am searching for a job in Computer Science.
Experience.SkillsText:
I've studied many different parts of programming, and have done so in a variety of programming languages. I am well-versed in both the practical and theoretical sides of Computer Science.

I have completed the Microsoft Azure Developer Associate certification, and so have knowledge of how to deploy web apps to that platform.

Project1.Title: Big Data Graph Traversal
Project1.Desc:
An team project for a class on algorithms (Over the winter quarter of 2025), this project assesses which nodes are most well suited to propagate an update across a given subnetwork of a modelled network. Programmed in Python and relying on the NetworkX framework to model the network as a graph, this project calculates the closeness centrality value of the nodes on the network to find the most appropriate one. Implemented rather naively, it does do the job it was meant to do... albeit with some inefficencies. The largest data set analyzed so far is a portion of Google's web graph. The data resulting from this process is outputted in the form of a graph generated by the MatPlotLib library.
I was the primary contributor to this project, and was responsible for resolving scheduling conflicts between team members. It was quite an interesting thing to work on, as I had not done anything similar in the past. My original attempt did not work as intended (I managed to both use the wrong equation and the wrong data type), so I had to do a few mid-development refactors to ensure the results reflected the data correctly.

Project2.Title: Seekr
Project2.Desc:
My senior capstone project, a three-quarters long collaboration with a small team over the 2025-2026 school year. Programmed in a mixture of HTML, CSS, and TypeScript (A variant of JavaScript that has stronger typing), this project provides a variety of functions helpful to any job seeker. It also uses the open source libraries ChartJS and react-calendar-heatmap to extend TypeScript's ability to display data.
Core features of this project include keeping a record of jobs applied to by the user, aggregating those records into graphs and statistics, providing autofill functionality on common job sites, and providing access to AI (Through the Firebase API and library) for the completion of complex fields.

I was a developer on this project, developing my skills by working on the backend database and the integration of the backend into the wider extension. I had no prior knowledge of TypeScript, so I had to rapidly learn how to apply my knowledge of JavaScript in a new format.
Our team alternated the role of Scrum Master between us, so I also learned how to perform the duties of that role.
